question: Will the UK increase the qualifying period for settlement to 10 years before May 2026?
summary: Ensemble suggests strong momentum toward a 10-year settlement baseline, with a plausible near-term rollout discussed to begin around April 2026.
Adversarial objections validly highlight lack of a fixed timetable, route-specific carve-outs, and policy uncertainty that reduce certainty about a universal 10-year baseline by May 2026.
Threshold analysis indicates a real possibility that some form of the 10-year baseline could be in effect for new applicants by May 2026, but full universal adoption is not guaranteed.
Anti-bias guard satisfied: adjustments are tied to policy feasibility and timetable uncertainty, not to physically implausible scenarios.

justification.critique_assessment: Objections are valid and reveal credible near-term uncertainties that justify lowering the probability from the ensemble figure.
justification.adjustment: Adjusted downward from 0.90 to 0.82 to reflect timetable uncertainty, phased rollout expectations, and carve-outs; no adjustment for implausible scenarios was applied.

forecasts.reference-class: UK immigration policy proposals to increase the standard settlement qualifying period (from 5 to 10 years) under the 2025 Earned Settlement/Immigration White Paper framework, with potential reductions or adjustments based on individual contributions and other criteria.

sources.claim: The consultation states the baseline qualifying period for settlement for most migrants will be increased from 5 to 10 years under an earned settlement model, with adjustments based on integration, contribution, and residence.

The government announced the doubling of the permanent settlement qualifying period to 10 years, with specific reductions for certain groups and penalties for others, as part of a major overhaul of the migration system.

The House of Commons Library notes the May 2025 white paper proposals include increasing the permanent residence/settlement qualifying period from 5 to 10 years, with no fixed timetable for implementation and potential April 2026 start for related rules.

Parliamentary debate records the government's plan to set a 10-year baseline for settlement and seek consultation on additional adjustments, implying near-term policy trajectory toward longer waiting periods.

The Guardian reports the immigration white paper proposed extending the settlement waiting period to 10 years for many migrants arriving since 2020, subject to consultation about transitional arrangements.
The consultation proposes increasing the baseline qualifying period for settlement to 10 years, with exceptions for certain groups; an earned settlement model is being considered.
The government outlined a baseline 10-year path to settlement with various route-specific exceptions; implementation would depend on subsequent policy decisions and legislation.

Migration Observatory summarizes a plan to raise the standard waiting period to 10 years for settlement, with certain routes exempt or shortened, and a broad set of factors affecting longer durations.
The immigration white paper signals a ten-year wait for settlement as the baseline, with earned settlement concepts and policy reforms under consultation.
Reporting suggests many migrants could face longer waits (up to 10 years or more) for permanent settlement under the proposed framework.
House of Commons Library notes the government proposes a baseline 10-year qualifying period for settlement, with exceptions.
GOV.UK consultation states the default qualifying period would increase to 10 years, with exceptions; outlines the earned settlement model.
Migration Observatory summaries indicate the standard waiting period would rise from five to ten years, with carve-outs; consultation open until Feb 12, 2026.
Littler notes the government launched an earned settlement consultation proposing a 10-year baseline with a phased rollout starting around April 2026.
Guardian reports government proposals to extend the wait for permanent settlement as part of broader immigration reform.
Financial Times coverage of reform proposals including extended settlement timelines and related immigration reforms.
